prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Scottish National Party Manifesto 2015 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core purpose
- Make Scotland’s voice stronger at Westminster; deliver a progressive alternative to austerity.
- Never put the Tories into power; work with an anti‑Tory majority to secure change across the UK.

Public finances and economy
- End austerity: modest annual real‑terms spending increases with deficit and debt falling as a share of GDP; balanced current budget over the medium term.
- Shift to investment-led growth: major infrastructure (transport, housing, broadband/4G), productivity and export support.
- Fairer taxation: restore 50p top rate; bank levy and bankers’ bonus tax; mansion tax; end non‑dom status; anti‑avoidance crackdown; review pension tax relief; create a sovereign wealth/energy fund.

Jobs, pay and business
- Minimum wage to £8.70 by 2020; promote the living wage via procurement and a Scottish Business Pledge.
- Raise Employment Allowance to £6,000 by 2019‑20; strengthen late‑payment protections for SMEs.
- Capitalise a Scottish Business Development Bank; expand export finance.
- Cut Air Passenger Duty by 50% (then abolish); review VAT cut for hospitality.
- Boost creative sector: fairer BBC Scotland funding (+£100m).

NHS, care and education
- Increase UK health spending, delivering an extra £2bn for NHS Scotland by 2020‑21; protect NHS from privatisation; expand mental health funding; integrate health and social care.
- Free tuition maintained; expand childcare to 30 hours/week for 3–4s and eligible 2s; 30,000 Modern Apprentices annually; expand EMA; £100m attainment fund.

Welfare and inequality
- Scrap Bedroom Tax; halt rollout of Universal Credit and PIP; reverse DLA-to-PIP change; benefits to rise at least with cost of living.
- Raise Universal Credit work allowance by 20%; overhaul sanctions and Work Capability Assessments.
- Increase Carer’s Allowance to JSA level (+~£600/year).
- Protect pensioner benefits; retain triple lock; single-tier pension at £160/week; review rise to state pension age 67.

Cost of living and housing
- Enforce energy bill cuts via Ofgem; fund ECO from general taxation; parity for prepayment customers; earlier winter fuel for off‑grid homes.
- UK target of 100,000 affordable homes/year; expand Scottish housebuilding.

Environment, energy and defence
- Strong climate targets; support offshore/onshore wind, hydro, CCS, community heat/energy; expand Green Investment Bank; moratorium on fracking.
- Oppose Trident renewal; publish full nuclear costs; strengthen Scotland’s conventional footprint (patrol vessels, maritime patrol aircraft); guarantee Type 26 build and carrier refit in Scotland; better veterans’ support.

Democracy, rights and policing
- More powers than Smith: employment law (incl. minimum wage), welfare, taxation, National Insurance, equality, broadcasting; move to full financial responsibility over time.
- EU: oppose withdrawal; require “double‑majority” in any referendum; protect public services from TTIP.
- Votes at 16; STV for Commons; abolish House of Lords; stronger MP recall; protect Human Rights Act/ECHR; oppose “snoopers’ charter”.
- Equality: 50% women on public boards; start equal pay audits; tighten maternity protections; abolish VAT on sanitary products.

Rural, communities and international
- Fair share of CAP convergence uplift; retain Royal Mail USO/public stake; devolve regulation of FOBTs and payday lending; direct Crown Estate seabed revenues to communities.
- International: keep aid at 0.7% GNI; audit developing‑country debt; two‑state solution for Israel/Palestine; create UK LGBTI rights envoy.

Political pledge
- SNP MPs will oppose any Westminster measure that harms Scotland’s interests or reduces its funding.
